chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If you give in charity a charity, it does not return to you, and you do not buy it back, except if you inherit it.

key_terms.تَرْجِعْ: Return, in the legal sense of reverting to ownership
key_terms.تَشْتَرِهَا: Buy it, referring to repurchasing the donated item
key_terms.تُورَثَ: Be inherited, the exception allowing return of ownership
key_terms.صَدَقَةٍ: Charity, a voluntary gift given for the sake of God

ai.seo_question: Can a donor buy back a charity they have already given?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal principle of 'ghabn' (alienation) in Islamic jurisprudence, establishing that a sadaqah, once given, is no longer the property of the donor and cannot be reclaimed or repurchased. The sole exception—inheritance—highlights the distinct mechanism by which ownership can revert through the natural succession of heirs rather than a direct transaction. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between simple gifts (hibah) and charitable endowments (sadaqah) regarding the donor's retained rights.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Mansour Bin Hazim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When you are given in charity with a charity, it does not return back to you, and you do not buy it except if you were to inherit it’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘ Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Mansur ibn Hazim who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If you give charity, then do not take it back or buy it back unless it comes back to you in the form of an inherited legacy.”’
